title: Ernie Andrews recording "Pastel" and "Primrose Lane"
summary: Callender explains the two titles of his song, Andrews's laid-back label and his belief that Andrews will make it big.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Mmm-hmm. Anyhow, Ernie Andrews recorded another tune of mine, "Pastel," which Erroll Garner recorded many years ago. So Ernie recorded it with the words. It had two titles. The first title was "Please Let Me Forget," and then "Pastel" was a subtitle. So Ernie recorded it, and since then I've changed the lyric to incorporate "Pastel"
into the lyric. But originally it was just "Please Let Me Forget."
Yeah, it's out now. But he never pushes anything; you know, it's just out there. If somebody happens to catch it, okay; if they don't, I don't think it bothers him at all.
Yeah, he's a very laid-back kind of record company owner.

Ernie called me the other day. He's doing another record date for him, and he's going to do my hit tune, "Primrose Lane." So he's going to do it, but I don't know if he's going to be with the company much longer. He's looking for a company that will push him. Now, here's a guy who, in my estimation, is one of the all-time greats who has never made it like he should. I just tell him, "Keep healthy; you'll make just like you want to."
Oh, he's a fine singer, a fine entertainer, and I think he's unlimited.
Yes. It's got to happen or him yet.
It will. It will happen big. All he has to do is to stay healthy.
